title: People’s Mañanera August 28
author: Pedro Gellert
content:
_Every day, President Claudia Sheinbaum gives a morning presidential press
conference and Mexico Solidarity Media posts English language summaries,
translated by Mexico Solidarity’s Pedro Gellert. Previous press conference
summaries are available[here](https://mexicosolidarity.com/mananera/)._

**Cabeza de Vaca Could Not Run for Office If He Is a Fugitive  
** Former Supreme Court Justice Arturo Zaldívar explained that if former
Tamaulipas Governor Francisco García Cabeza de Vaca has a pending arrest
warrant and remains outside the country to evade justice, he is a fugitive and
cannot run for office. An arrest warrant alone is not sufficient; it must be
proven that he has evaded justice.

**More Screening Measures to Block Criminals from Running for Office  
** By 2027, political parties will be able to voluntarily request that the
National Electoral Institute (INE) review information on their pre-candidates,
those who seek their nomination to run for public office. The INE will consult
with the Federal Attorney General’s Office (FGR), the Financial Intelligence
Unit (UIF), and Security to identify potential candidates’ possible risks or
criminal ties.

**García Luna’s Multi-Million-Dollar Scheme Before the Courts  
** Between 2008 and 2018, companies linked to former Minister of Public
Security Genaro García Luna received more than US$403 million. The UIF
reported the case in 2019: there were 61 arrest warrants served, 17 arrests
made, and a judgment issued for US$578.5 million against the Weinberg family,
García Luna’s business partners.

**What Was Taken From the People Returns to the People  
** Mexico recovered nearly 100 million pesos (US$5.89 million) from the García
Luna-Weinberg case, and it was announced that the funds will be used to
improve schools in the Montaña region of Guerrero. It was noted that the case
helps “expose the hypocrisy” of those who defended García Luna.

**From Calderón’s War to Peacebuilding  
** President Claudia Sheinbaum recalled that under ex-president Felipe
Calderón, homicides rose from 27 to more than 70 per day and asked: “What does
‘war’ mean? They were exceptional circumstances […] there was a license to
kill.” Today, crime is combated through justice and by addressing its root
causes.

**Mexican Talent Makes History on the World Stage  
** Sheinbaum congratulated Kenia Lechuga on winning the gold medal at the
World Rowing Championship in Amsterdam. The President acknowledged the
promotion of high-performance sports and the international achievements of
children in mathematics and robotics.
